goal:
Implement cursor.nvim per the repository implementation plan.

The v0.1 baseline already shipped directly on cursor/orchestrate-cursor-nvim-e603 because CURSOR_API_KEY was unavailable when the planner first booted (see .orchestrate/cursor-nvim/attention.log). The substrate now has the key, so the remaining orchestrate work is: independently verify the v0.1 deliverable against IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and add a single feature increment that proves a real fan-out worked.

Workers read IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md at the repo root for full v0.1 scope.
summary: verify cursor.nvim v0.1 + add :CursorVersion (orchestrate substrate smoke test)
acceptanceCriteria: verify-v0-1 produces a Verification line of unit-test-verified or stronger against IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md acceptance criteria
add-version-command ships :CursorVersion + a test, on its own worker branch with a clean handoff

tasks.name: add-version-command
tasks.scopedGoal: Add a small feature increment to cursor.nvim that proves a real worker fan-out worked: a :CursorVersion ex command that prints `cursor.nvim vX.Y.Z` to :messages, where the version is read from a single Lua constant (lua/cursor/version.lua exposing M = '0.1.0'). Wire it into plugin/cursor.lua exactly like the existing :CursorStatus command (lazy-loaded via require('cursor')). Update lua/cursor/init.lua to expose require('cursor').version() returning the constant. Add a plenary spec at lua/cursor/_spec/version_spec.lua asserting that (a) require('cursor').version() == '0.1.0' (or whatever the constant says — read it dynamically); (b) :CursorVersion is registered. Update README.md and doc/cursor.txt to document :CursorVersion under the existing command tables. Run `make lint && make test` (after `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/nvim-lua/plenary.nvim .deps/plenary.nvim`) and only hand off when both are green. Push to your own branch.
acceptance: lua/cursor/version.lua exists and exports a single string constant
:CursorVersion is registered and prints `cursor.nvim v<version>` to :messages
require('cursor').version() returns the same string the constant exports
lua/cursor/_spec/version_spec.lua has at least 2 assertions and passes under PlenaryBustedDirectory
stylua --check lua/ plugin/ and luacheck lua/ plugin/ both pass
README.md and doc/cursor.txt mention :CursorVersion in their command tables
tasks.verify:
## Setup
- git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/nvim-lua/plenary.nvim .deps/plenary.nvim

## Automated
- make lint
- make test

## Manual
- nvim --headless --noplugin -u tests/minimal_init.lua -c "CursorVersion" -c "qa!" prints `cursor.nvim v<version>` to stdout via :messages.

## Gotchas
- Don't touch agent.lua, health.lua, config.lua, ui/*, or CI — those are out of bounds. The point of this task is a clean diff that exercises the orchestrate spawn-handoff loop end-to-end.

tasks.name: verify-v0-1
tasks.scopedGoal: Verify the cursor.nvim v0.1 deliverable on the add-version-command branch (which carries the v0.1 baseline plus the new :CursorVersion command). Read IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and verify every acceptance bullet from the v0.1 'Acceptance criteria for v0.1' section, plus the add-version-command bullets. Steps: (1) sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends neovim luarocks (Neovim 0.9 is sufficient for the spec suite); (2) sudo luarocks install luacheck; (3) curl -fsSL https://github.com/JohnnyMorganz/StyLua/releases/latest/download/stylua-linux-x86_64.zip -o /tmp/stylua.zip && cd /tmp && unzip -o stylua.zip && chmod +x stylua && sudo mv stylua /usr/local/bin/; (4) git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/nvim-lua/plenary.nvim .deps/plenary.nvim; (5) make lint; (6) make test; (7) nvim --headless --noplugin -u tests/minimal_init.lua -c "lua require('cursor').setup({notify=false})" -c "lua local c = vim.api.nvim_get_commands({}); for _,n in ipairs({'CursorChat','CursorAsk','CursorStop','CursorStatus','CursorVersion'}) do assert(c[n], n .. ' missing') end print('COMMANDS_OK')" -c "qa!". Report a Verification line of unit-test-verified if make test is green and commands register, type-check-only if only stylua/luacheck pass, verifier-blocked if env install fails, verifier-failed if any acceptance bullet does not hold. Per-criterion findings must cite the actual command output you saw.
acceptance: Verification section reports per-criterion pass/fail with execution evidence (real command output, not paraphrased)
Verification line is one of unit-test-verified / type-check-only / verifier-blocked / verifier-failed
